title: Punam Raut Retires After Career Defined by 2017 World Cup Final
excerpt: The India opener ends an international career spanning 2009 to 2021 with 2,299 ODI runs, a record 320-run opening stand with Deepti Sharma, and a top-scoring 86 in the 2017 World Cup final.
body:
• Punam Raut, 37, has retired from international cricket with immediate effect, ending an India career that ran from 2009 to 2021.
  • She played 4 Tests, 73 ODIs and 35 T20Is, scoring 2,299 ODI runs at 34.83 with three centuries and 15 half-centuries.
  • Her defining tournament was the 2017 World Cup: 381 runs, a century against Australia, and a top-scoring 86 in the final against England at Lord's.
  • With Deepti Sharma she shared a record 320-run opening stand against Ireland in Potchefstroom in 2017.

India top-order batter Punam Raut has announced her retirement from all forms of international cricket with immediate effect. Raut, who turned 37 on Wednesday, represented India from 2009 to 2021, playing four Tests, 73 one-day internationals and 35 Twenty20 internationals, according to ESPNcricinfo.

Announcing the decision on Instagram, Raut said representing India had been the greatest honour of her life and that the game had shaped her character and taught her resilience. She thanked the Mumbai Cricket Association for backing her during her formative years.

A Career Built in One-Day Cricket

Raut was most prolific in the 50-over format. She scored 2,299 ODI runs at an average of 34.83, with three centuries and 15 half-centuries. In T20 internationals she made 719 runs at 27.65, striking at 92.17, with four half-centuries across 35 matches, Cricbuzz reported. Her four Tests brought 264 runs, including a century — 130 against South Africa at Mysore in 2014 — after she had begun her Test career with a duck.

She appeared in three ODI World Cups, in 2009, 2013 and 2017, and four T20 World Cups, in 2009, 2010, 2012 and 2014. Her T20 World Cup highlights included a match-winning unbeaten 54 against Pakistan in 2009 and 56 off 52 balls against West Indies in 2014.

2017: The Tournament That Defined Her

Raut herself called the 2017 World Cup a defining moment, saying the tournament transformed women's cricket in India and inspired a generation of young players, even though India fell just short of the trophy. The numbers support the claim. She scored 381 runs in that tournament, including a century in a league game against Australia, and top-scored with 86 in the final against England at Lord's, which India lost by nine runs.

"The 2017 ICC Women's Cricket World Cup will always remain one of the defining moments of my career."

— Punam Raut

Earlier that year, in Potchefstroom, Raut and Deepti Sharma put on a record opening stand of 320 runs against Ireland in an ODI. Raut retired hurt on 109 off 116 balls while Deepti scored 188 off 160 — a partnership that still stands as a landmark in the women's game.

Walking, and a Final Test

Raut's last appearance for India was the drawn Test against Australia at Carrara in 2021, where she scored 36 and an unbeaten 41. That match, India's historic pink-ball Test, also produced the moment many fans remember her for off the scoresheet: she walked after edging a delivery despite being given not out, earning widespread praise for her sportsmanship.

What She Leaves Behind

Raut has not played for India since 2021, so the announcement formalises the end of a career that had already moved into its next phase. In her retirement message she said she intends to give back to the game that gave her a purpose and an identity — closing a chapter that began on the streets of Mumbai and reached a World Cup final at Lord's.
